cards.title: Set bidding strategy to your business constraint, not a trend
cards.summary: Pick auto bidding or manual caps based on the specific constraint in the store's ad account rather than adopting whatever manual bidding method is currently popular.
cards.use_when: Reviewing bidding strategy across a portfolio of campaigns or when a scaling campaign needs a guardrail on CPA.

cards.title: Push broad control to its limit, but audit Meta's suggestions
cards.summary: Give Meta enough control to let the algorithm work, but systematically reject automated recommendations that are not backed by your own account data.
cards.use_when: Reviewing Meta's automated recommendations and Advantage+ suggestions before applying them to a live store account.

cards.title: Attribute conversions outside Facebook and read conversion data sceptically
cards.summary: Post-click conversion reporting inside Facebook is unreliable after iOS tracking changes, so judge performance with third-party attribution while still sending Meta good signal.
cards.use_when: Deciding which numbers to trust when reporting store performance or judging whether a Meta campaign is actually profitable.

cards.title: Send first-party signal via the Conversions API even when attribution is uncertain
cards.summary: Server-side event sending improves the data Meta learns from, so implement it as hygiene while keeping your trust in Facebook-reported conversions low.
cards.use_when: Setting up or auditing a store's Meta tracking foundation before scaling spend.

cards.title: Model every ad against the three takeaways of the auction
cards.summary: Creative acts as targeting, strong soft metrics supply half the total value equation, and respecting user experience protects long-term delivery.
cards.use_when: Briefing creative or auditing an account structure before committing budget to a store's next campaign push.

cards.title: Treat ad rejections and ban waves as timing and account scale, not pure fault
cards.summary: Meta's enforcement tightens or loosens around business cycles, so identical creative can be approved for one advertiser and rejected for another.
cards.use_when: Planning risk mitigation for a store's ad account, page or business manager after a rejection or ban.

cards.title: Treat facebook internally reported numbers as untrusted until externally verified
cards.summary: The presenter argues that Facebook is a for-profit company that optimizes for the most revenue from the largest advertisers, so internal platform metrics and recommendations should not be treated as neutral guidance.
cards.use_when: Reviewing performance reports or vendor claims for a store's Meta spend, or deciding how much weight to give Meta's own optimization scores when making budgeting decisions.

cards.title: Build a Four-Layer Google Ads Retail Stack
cards.summary: Architect ecommerce Google Ads as parallel Standard Shopping, PMax, Demand Gen and brand campaigns with explicit roles rather than one campaign type.
cards.use_when: Structuring or restructuring the whole Google Ads account for an ecommerce catalog: deciding which campaign types to run and what job each one does.

cards.title: Standard Shopping for SKU-Level Bid Control
cards.summary: Use Standard Shopping when you need product-group bid control, clear per-product query data and read-clean conversions that PMax blurs.
cards.use_when: Deciding which products belong in Standard Shopping versus PMax, or when PMax reporting is too blended to tell what is actually working.

cards.title: Choose Feed-Only vs Full-Asset PMax for Retail
cards.summary: Test a feed-led retail PMax configuration against the store baseline without assuming strict audience or channel isolation.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a feed-led versus full-asset Performance Max campaign for an ecommerce product catalog.

cards.title: Structure PMax Asset Groups by Theme for Retail
cards.summary: Segment PMax asset groups by product category or performance tier instead of one generic group, and refresh creative on a cadence.
cards.use_when: Building PMax asset groups for a product catalog, or when a single generic asset group is producing weak or inconsistent results.

cards.title: Use Demand Gen for Feed-Powered Mid-Funnel Retail
cards.summary: Deploy Demand Gen with product feed integration when you need placement-level creative control and upper-funnel demand creation that PMax automates away.
cards.use_when: Planning mid-funnel or upper-funnel YouTube/Discover coverage for an ecommerce catalog, or when you need distinct creative per placement rather than AI-combined assets.

cards.title: Match YouTube Ad Formats to Ecommerce Jobs
cards.summary: Pick YouTube formats by the ecommerce task each performs, from 6-second bumpers to feed placements for catalog browsing.
cards.use_when: Selecting video ad formats and lengths for a Demand Gen or PMax campaign in an ecommerce account.

cards.title: Stop PMax Brand Cannibalisation in Retail Accounts
cards.summary: Apply three parallel controls so PMax cannot absorb branded demand and inflate reported ROAS.
cards.use_when: Diagnosing suspiciously strong PMax ROAS, or setting up a new ecommerce account where branded search must stay separately measured.

cards.title: Read the Shopping and PMax Auction Correctly
cards.summary: In Shopping and PMax there are no keywords — quality signals come from feed data, so product titles and attributes drive Ad Rank.
cards.use_when: Explaining why a product wins or loses Shopping auctions, or deciding where to invest to improve visibility and CPC.

cards.title: Rewrite Product Titles with Attribute Front-Loading
cards.summary: Front-load the attributes buyers search for in the first ~70 characters of product titles instead of leading with the brand and product name.
cards.use_when: Optimising product titles in Google Merchant Center for Shopping, PMax or Demand Gen visibility on a retail catalog.

cards.title: Use Supplemental Feeds and Feed Duplication by Campaign Role
cards.summary: Override feed fields without touching the website, and duplicate the feed so Standard Shopping and PMax each get a role-matched version.
cards.use_when: Testing title variants, applying promotional labels, or running Shopping and PMax in parallel on the same catalog.

cards.title: Run a Feed Health Diagnostic and Disapproval Triage
cards.summary: Work Merchant Center Diagnostics by severity, fix high-revenue problems first, and pre-validate to stop errors reaching Google.
cards.use_when: Weekly or monthly catalog hygiene for an ecommerce store running Shopping, PMax or free listings, or after a sudden drop in eligible products.

cards.title: Build Ecommerce Conversion Tracking via GTM
cards.summary: Layer Conversion Linker, GA4 purchase event and Google Ads conversion tags, and pass product-level dynamic remarketing parameters.
cards.use_when: Setting up or auditing conversion tracking for a Shopify or WooCommerce store before scaling Google Ads spend.

cards.title: Turn On Enhanced Conversions to Feed Smart Bidding
cards.summary: Send hashed first-party customer data with conversion tags to improve match rates and give Smart Bidding enough signal to learn.
cards.use_when: Ecommerce accounts with low purchase volume relative to lead-gen accounts, or any store where Smart Bidding appears starved of conversion signal.

cards.title: Pass Real Order Revenue to Target ROAS Bidding
cards.summary: Send actual order values including discounts and shipping server-side, because tROAS can only hit your target if conversion values are accurate.
cards.use_when: Configuring conversion values for an ecommerce store running Target ROAS or Maximize Conversion Value bidding.

cards.title: Tier Ecommerce Keyword Research by Buyer Intent
cards.summary: Organise search campaigns into four intent tiers — transactional, comparison, problem-aware and competitor — each with its own bid and landing page logic.
cards.use_when: Building or restructuring Search campaigns for an ecommerce store, or deciding which queries deserve their own ad groups and budgets.

cards.title: Separate Brand and Non-Brand Budgets for Honest ROAS
cards.summary: Split brand and non-brand into separate campaigns, budgets and reporting so you can tell whether prospecting actually pays.
cards.use_when: Reviewing account-level ROAS for an ecommerce store, or planning how much budget to shift from brand defence into category and problem-aware prospecting.

cards.title: Scale with Surface-Area Catalog Logic
cards.summary: Give Shopping and PMax enough catalog breadth and feed segmentation to find profitable demand pockets, and structure campaigns around commercial reality.
cards.use_when: Planning growth for a Google Ads ecommerce account, especially when deciding whether catalog size or campaign structure is the bottleneck.

cards.title: Set Target ROAS and Maximize Conversion Value Guardrails
cards.summary: Start tROAS below current performance, step up slowly, and use Maximize Conversion Value when you will accept lower marginal ROAS for volume.
cards.use_when: Choosing or tuning bid strategies for ecommerce Shopping and PMax campaigns, or revalidating legacy targets after the August 2026 behaviour change.

cards.title: Use Portfolio Bid Strategies for Caps and Floors
cards.summary: Pool campaigns under one strategy to share learning and gain Max CPC caps and bid floors that standalone Smart Bidding does not offer.
cards.use_when: Running multiple ecommerce campaigns toward the same performance goal, or when Smart Bidding causes CPC spikes that threaten budget control.

cards.title: Pass Five Gates Before Scaling Ecommerce Spend
cards.summary: Sequence scaling behind feed health, tracking integrity, brand separation, creative velocity and bid-strategy maturity — fix inputs before chasing outputs.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to increase budget or add campaign types in an ecommerce Google Ads account.

cards.title: Choose Between PMax, Shopping and Demand Gen by Job
cards.summary: Match campaign type to the job — multi-surface acquisition, Shopping-surface precision, or upper-funnel demand creation — and keep them from competing.
cards.use_when: Assigning budget and roles across Google Ads campaign types for an ecommerce catalog as the account grows.

cards.title: Anchor ROAS Targets to Margin, Not Benchmarks
cards.summary: Use 2026 ecommerce ROAS/CPC benchmarks only as context, and set targets relative to gross margin, AOV and vertical economics.
cards.use_when: Setting or defending a target ROAS for an ecommerce account, or benchmarking account performance against market figures.

cards.title: Four-Layer Google Ads Account Model for Ecommerce
cards.summary: Stack AI Max Search, Performance Max, Demand Gen and branded/non-brand Search so each layer feeds the next instead of running as isolated campaigns.
cards.use_when: You are architecting or restructuring a full Google Ads account (typically $50K–$500K/month spend) and deciding which campaign types to run and how they relate.

cards.title: Feed-Only Performance Max for a Feed-Led Retail Test
cards.summary: Test a feed-led retail PMax configuration against the store baseline without assuming strict audience or channel isolation.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a feed-led versus full-asset Performance Max campaign for an ecommerce product catalog.

cards.title: Stop PMax and Shopping Cannibalising Brand Demand
cards.summary: Three parallel fixes — brand negatives on PMax, negatives on new-customer campaigns, and dedicated branded campaigns — keep PMax from eating the highest-intent commercial traffic.
cards.use_when: PMax and Shopping run against the same feed and you suspect PMax is absorbing branded and high-intent queries, destroying cost transparency on your most valuable searches.

cards.title: Configure Demand Gen as the Assist Layer
cards.summary: Run Demand Gen prospecting and remarketing separately, feed it continuous creative, and scale bids in small increments to build the awareness layer that PMax and Search later convert.
cards.use_when: You need a top-of-funnel demand-creation layer in Google Ads and are setting up Demand Gen campaigns, structure, bidding and pacing for ecommerce.

cards.title: Match YouTube Ad Formats to Funnel Stage
cards.summary: Choose among Skippable In-Stream, In-Feed, Non-Skippable, Bumper, Shorts and Masthead based on placement, length cap and funnel job, and note which campaign types can serve each format.
cards.use_when: You are planning video assets for a Google Ads stack and must decide which format to produce and which campaign type to run it in.

cards.title: How the Google Ads Auction Actually Works
cards.summary: Every search runs a millisecond auction where bid is only one input alongside auction-time quality, asset impact, competitiveness and user context — so outspending does not lock top positions.
cards.use_when: You are diagnosing why a higher bid is not winning position, or explaining to a stakeholder why budget alone cannot buy placement.

cards.title: Ad Rank Formula and Position Threshold Heuristics
cards.summary: Ad Rank = Max CPC Bid × Quality Score × Expected Impact of Extensions/Formats + Contextual Adjustments, calculated twice per auction, with source-quoted position thresholds.
cards.use_when: You are estimating how much bid headroom you need for top-of-page or top-3 placement, or modelling whether raising Quality Score beats raising bids.

cards.title: Use Quality Score as a Diagnostic, Not a Currency
cards.summary: The visible 1–10 Quality Score aggregates auction-time signals and is not read directly by the auction; expected CTR and landing page experience each carry roughly 39% of the weighting.
cards.use_when: You are prioritising between ad copy testing and landing page work to improve Quality Score and reduce CPC.

cards.title: Second-Price Logic: Why Higher Quality Lowers Actual CPC
cards.summary: You pay the minimum needed to beat the advertiser below you — Actual CPC = (Ad Rank below you ÷ Your Quality Score) + $0.01 — so Quality Score appears in the denominator.
cards.use_when: You are justifying investment in ad relevance and landing page quality to reduce cost per click, or explaining why a competitor with a bigger bid pays more for a worse position.

cards.title: Smart Bidding Basics, Relabelling and Seasonality Adjustments
cards.summary: Smart Bidding sets a bid in every individual auction using real-time signals; 2026 relabelled tCPA/tROAS as standalone strategies, and seasonality adjustments are for short predictable-only deviations of 1–7 days.
cards.use_when: You are choosing a bid strategy, interpreting the 2026 strategy labels, or deciding whether to apply a seasonality adjustment around a promotion.

cards.title: Treat the Product Feed as the Advertising Copy
cards.summary: In Shopping and PMax there are no keywords — Google reads your feed title, description, attributes, price and availability to decide which queries each product matches.
cards.use_when: You are optimising Google Shopping or Performance Max for ecommerce and deciding where to spend merchandising and copywriting effort.

cards.title: Product Title Architecture for Feed Matching
cards.summary: Use Product Type → Material → Colour → Fit/Size → Key Feature → Brand (last), keeping titles 60–150 characters with the match-driving attributes inside the first ~70 characters.
cards.use_when: You are writing or rewriting product titles for a Google Merchant Center feed to improve query matching in Shopping and PMax.

cards.title: Feed Health Diagnostics and Disapproval Remediation
cards.summary: Work Google Merchant Center Diagnostics from Disapproved to Warnings to Limited performance, use Autofix for low-risk issues, and pre-validate before Google sees the feed.
cards.use_when: You are doing routine Google Merchant Center maintenance or fixing disapprovals that are costing you Shopping and free-listing eligibility.

cards.title: Conversion Tracking Tag Architecture via GTM
cards.summary: Layer a Conversion Linker tag, a GA4 event tag and a Google Ads Conversion Tracking tag, with server-side GTM to move tags off the browser and hard-code tracking in Ads templates rather than Merchant Center.
cards.use_when: You are setting up or auditing Google Ads conversion tracking for an ecommerce store, including checkout purchase events.

cards.title: Enhanced Conversions Setup and Diagnostics
cards.summary: Send hashed first-party customer data from your site to supplement standard conversion tags, improving measurement and bidding; from April 2026 Google accepts data from web tags, Data Manager and API simultaneously.
cards.use_when: You are improving ecommerce conversion measurement accuracy or diagnosing why conversion counts look undercounted versus backend orders.

cards.title: Server-Side Tracking for Page Speed and Data Durability
cards.summary: Server-side GTM improves page speed, survives browser privacy restrictions better, and allows enrichment with CRM/backend signals — increasingly the default above $50K/month spend.
cards.use_when: You are evaluating whether to move conversion tracking server-side, or troubleshooting declining measured conversions in ecommerce.

cards.title: Intent-Tiered Keyword Research Workflow
cards.summary: Organise keywords into transactional, comparison, problem-aware and competitor tiers — each with its own bids, landing pages, measurement and negative keyword coverage.
cards.use_when: You are planning or restructuring a Search campaign's keyword strategy for an ecommerce store.

cards.title: Brand vs Non-Brand Segmentation and ROAS Distortion
cards.summary: Brand traffic captures demand and non-brand creates it; blending the two flatters account ROAS and hides whether prospecting is actually profitable.
cards.use_when: You are deciding how to split budget and reporting between brand and non-brand Search/Shopping, or diagnosing suspiciously stable account-level ROAS.

cards.title: Surface-Area Catalog Scaling with Feed Duplication
cards.summary: Algorithmic opportunity scales with catalog breadth; duplicate the feed with role-specific rules so Shopping and PMax each surface products more often without hurting efficiency.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether you have enough catalog to scale Shopping/PMax, or looking for a way to increase impressions without raising bids.

cards.title: Target ROAS vs Maximize Conversion Value
cards.summary: Use Target ROAS when conversion values vary and you need a return floor; use Maximize Conversion Value when you accept lower marginal ROAS during growth — start tROAS 10–15% below current actual ROAS.
cards.use_when: You are selecting a bid strategy for a Shopping or PMax campaign and setting the initial tROAS value.

cards.title: Portfolio Bid Strategies for Stabilised Scale and Bid Guardrails
cards.summary: Group campaigns under one automated strategy to share learning and reallocate budget, and access bid caps/floors only available through portfolio bidding.
cards.use_when: You have multiple campaigns chasing the same ROAS or CPA goal, or you need a Max CPC cap to stop Smart Bidding budget blowouts.

cards.title: Five Gates Before Scaling Google Ads Spend
cards.summary: Fix five inputs — feed health, conversion tracking integrity, brand/non-brand separation, creative velocity and bid strategy maturity — before chasing output volume.
cards.use_when: You are deciding whether to increase budget or scale campaigns, or diagnosing why a scaled campaign underperformed.

cards.title: Map Google Ads campaign types to funnel stage before allocating budget
cards.summary: Six Google Ads campaign types (Search, Shopping, Display, Demand Gen, Video, PMax) each sit at a different funnel stage and should be launched in a specific order.
cards.use_when: Deciding which Google Ads campaign types to launch first when moving budget over from Meta or building a new Google account for a DTC store.

cards.title: Split branded and non-branded Search/Shopping to protect and grow
cards.summary: Branded campaigns defend traffic and cheaply feed the algorithm; non-branded campaigns are where new-customer growth actually happens.
cards.use_when: Structuring Search and Shopping campaigns for a store, particularly when deciding how much budget to put behind the brand name versus generic product queries.

cards.title: Use a feed-only Performance Max campaign as a feed-led retail test
cards.summary: Test a feed-led retail PMax configuration against the store baseline without assuming strict audience or channel isolation.
cards.use_when: Evaluating a feed-led versus full-asset Performance Max campaign for an ecommerce product catalog.

cards.title: Run Display remarketing against exact previously-viewed products
cards.summary: Display campaigns are strongest for remarketing, and when tagged correctly they can show shoppers the exact products they viewed or carted.
cards.use_when: Setting up retargeting for a store where shoppers browse product pages or add to cart but do not purchase.

cards.title: Use Demand Gen to create demand on YouTube Shorts, Discover and Gmail
cards.summary: Demand Gen blends image and video ads across YouTube Shorts, the Discover feed and Gmail promotions to reach people who are not actively searching yet.
cards.use_when: Planning top-funnel paid acquisition to reach cold or in-market audiences on Google's non-search surfaces, or looking for a cheaper video placement than Instagram Reels.

cards.title: Match YouTube ad format to the job the video needs to do
cards.summary: YouTube offers Shorts, bumper, skippable in-stream, non-skippable in-stream and in-feed formats, each with different length, skip rules and placements.
cards.use_when: Choosing which YouTube video ad format to produce and buy for a store's awareness, consideration or retargeting objective.

cards.title: Set the core Google Ads columns and read them in the right order
cards.summary: A consistent column set — impressions, clicks, CTR, cost, conv. value/cost, CPA, conversions, avg CPC, conversion rate — makes campaign health readable at a glance.
cards.use_when: Configuring the Google Ads campaign view so you can judge performance daily without digging through reports.

cards.title: Judge CTR only against its campaign type, not one universal benchmark
cards.summary: Acceptable click-through rate varies enormously by campaign type, so use the source's loose ranges only as directional checks.
cards.use_when: Reviewing Search or Shopping ad copy and targeting, or diagnosing whether a campaign's click-through is genuinely weak.

cards.title: Understand conversion lag with conversions vs conversions-by-conversion-time
cards.summary: Google credits conversions to the ad-click date by default, while 'by conversion time' reports the date the purchase actually happened — the gap is conversion lag.
cards.use_when: Reading weekly or recent Google Ads performance for any store with a non-impulsive consideration phase, before deciding a campaign is failing.

cards.title: Read impression share to find out whether budget or ad rank is capping you
cards.summary: Search impression share splits what you missed into lost-to-rank and lost-to-budget, telling you which lever to pull.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether to raise budget or improve ad quality when a Search campaign is not serving as often as it could.

cards.title: Diagnose ad rank through quality score's three components
cards.summary: Quality score (out of 10) is driven by expected CTR, landing page experience and ad relevance — improve those before paying more per click.
cards.use_when: Improving an underperforming Search campaign that is losing impression share to rank, rather than simply increasing bids.

cards.title: Use video metrics: impressions vs views, view rate, CPV and frequency
cards.summary: Video campaigns report views, view rate, average CPV, CPM, video-played-to percentages, watch time and impression frequency — with 'view' defined differently per format.
cards.use_when: Evaluating YouTube or video campaign creative performance and deciding whether the hook or the targeting is at fault.

cards.title: Build custom columns for ROAS-by-time, device splits and average daily spend
cards.summary: Custom columns let you surface a specific formula — most usefully conversion-value-by-conversion-time ÷ cost — directly in the campaign view.
cards.use_when: Reporting on Google Ads for a store with a long consideration phase, or comparing mobile vs desktop performance at a glance.

cards.title: Link GA4 to Google Ads via Admin → Product links, then demote the imported purchase action
cards.summary: Connecting GA4 and Google Ads enables importing GA4 audiences and conversion actions — but the imported purchase action must be set to secondary to avoid double counting.
cards.use_when: Setting up GA4-to-Google-Ads reporting and audience imports for a Shopify store, or auditing an account whose ROAS suddenly doubled after linking analytics.

cards.title: Use four GA4 reports to sanity-check paid traffic quality
cards.summary: User attributes, monetization purchases, landing pages and channel reports give an ecommerce operator a quick outside-view of what paid traffic is doing on site.
cards.use_when: Reviewing store traffic quality every couple of weeks, especially to see how paid landing pages and channels are performing beyond Google Ads' own numbers.

cards.title: Build a 30-day cart-abandoner audience in GA4 and import it to Google Ads
cards.summary: Include users who triggered add-to-cart in the last 30 days and exclude purchasers, then import the audience for specific cart-recovery remarketing.
cards.use_when: Setting up cart-abandonment retargeting for a store, or creating a high-intent audience for Google Ads remarketing campaigns.

cards.title: Fix conversion tracking before anything else — it feeds you and the algorithm
cards.summary: Without correct conversion tracking both you and Google's automated bidding are blind, making every other optimisation moot.
cards.use_when: Starting Google Ads for a store, or auditing an account that is running automated bid strategies on unreliable conversion data.

cards.title: Consolidate everything under one master Google account
cards.summary: Using a single Google account linked to Ads, Merchant Center and Analytics prevents broken connections and duplicated setup.
cards.use_when: Setting up or cleaning up a store's Google ecosystem before connecting Shopify, Merchant Center feeds or GA4.

cards.title: Adopt Google Ads as the stability layer under Meta-led acquisition
cards.summary: The source's positioning is that Google Ads should be the reliable, always-on acquisition backbone for DTC brands rather than the flashiest channel.
cards.use_when: Deciding whether and why to diversify a Meta-dependent store into Google, and how to frame the channel's role internally.

cards.title: Threshold the switch from Maximize Clicks to value-based bidding
cards.summary: Move bidding from Maximize Clicks (data gathering) to Maximize Conversion Value or Target ROAS once you reach 15–30 conversions per month.
cards.use_when: Choosing a bid strategy for a new or low-volume Google Ads campaign, and deciding when to graduate to automated value bidding.

cards.title: Connect Shopify to Google Ads via the Google & YouTube App
cards.summary: Centralize your Google account and link Shopify to Google Ads so Shopify API conversion actions import automatically.
cards.use_when: Initial Google Ads setup or account audit for a Shopify store that has no working conversion tracking.

cards.title: Set Exactly One Primary Purchase Action
cards.summary: Avoid double-counted revenue from having two primary purchase actions, and fix action optimization settings.
cards.use_when: Auditing or setting up conversion tracking, or when your reported ROAS and revenue look implausibly strong.

cards.title: Use Cart Abandoners as a Remarketing Audience
cards.summary: Build a GA4 cart-abandoner audience that excludes buyers, import it into Google Ads, and only launch it once list size qualifies.
cards.use_when: Setting up remarketing for potential buyers who added to cart but did not purchase, especially for retention and checkout-stage recovery.

cards.title: Create Website Visitor Remarketing Lists by Page Depth
cards.summary: Build Google Ads website-visitor audiences in Audience Manager and decide whether to target all pages or specific product and collection URLs.
cards.use_when: Creating remarketing audiences for abandoned-browse recovery, dynamic remarketing, or any retargeting by page intent.

cards.title: Build YouTube Interactor Lists to Sequence Education into Direct Response
cards.summary: Create YouTube user remarketing segments based on specific videos watched, then remarket educational top-of-funnel viewers with direct-response creative.
cards.use_when: Designing acquisition creative strategy that sequences YouTube awareness content into purchase-driven retargeting.

cards.title: Upload Customer Lists for Signals, Lookalikes and Exclusion
cards.summary: Upload a hashed customer CSV to Google Ads to feed audience signals, build lookalikes in Demand Gen, and exclude existing buyers from campaigns.
cards.use_when: Acquisition expansion, lookalike targeting, or excluding existing customers from non-branded and general campaigns.

cards.title: Build Custom Segments from Search Terms to Find New Demand Pockets
cards.summary: Use Google Ads custom segments based on searched terms, competitor or similar websites, and overlapping interest to dial in targeting and scale into new audiences.
cards.use_when: Opening new prospecting pockets, tuning acquisition targeting, or reaching problem-aware shoppers before they search your category terms.

cards.title: Set Up Google Merchant Center and Sync Products for Shopping Ads
cards.summary: Create or link a Merchant Center account through the Shopify app, sync products, and connect it to Google Ads to unlock Shopping ads, free listings and local inventory ads.
cards.use_when: Before launching Shopping campaigns, or when your Shopify products are not feeding into Google Ads.

cards.title: Map Product Feed Attributes to Search Intent in Shopping Campaigns
cards.summary: Because Shopping campaigns have no keyword targeting, improve the five highest-impact feed attributes — price, title, images, descriptions and GTINs — so products serve on the closest-match queries.
cards.use_when: Feed optimization for Shopping campaigns, especially when products serve on irrelevant queries or conversions lag.
